annotationRationale: Prime exponents determine integrality. Negative integer exponents explain the denominator obstruction, and counting integers in the resulting interval finishes the solution.
sourceMethod: Follows the official prime-factorization argument, explicitly explaining why powers of distinct primes cannot cancel a negative exponent.

review.mathCheck: Factoring gives 2^(5+n)·5^(3−n). Distinct primes cannot cancel a negative exponent, so integrality is equivalent to −5≤n≤3. Both endpoints work, giving 9 integers, choice E.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 7 on page 3. It preserves the prime-exponent argument and inclusive count while explicitly explaining the uncanceled denominator.
review.annotationCheck: Prime-exponent integrality is correctly assessed; negative exponents and integer-interval counting appropriately support the method.
